extracted.intended_audience: Department of Transportation staff and Operating Administrations (OAs); project sponsors, environmental review practitioners, and public stakeholders who prepare or comment on DOT NEPA documents
extracted.subtask_description: Revision of DOT Order 5610.1C to modernize Department-wide NEPA implementing procedures, align them with the FRA 2023 statutory amendments, relevant executive actions and court precedent, and to promote more efficient, predictable, and streamlined environmental reviews across DOT and its Operating Administrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity with amended NEPA statute and recent legal developments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order revises DOT's NEPA implementing procedures to conform to the 2023 statutory amendments (FRA 2023), recent Executive Orders (e.g., E.O. 14154), and relevant Supreme Court decisions (e.g., Seven County), and to proceed now that CEQ implementing regulations have been rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOT must align its procedures with statutory amendments that altered scope, alternatives, page/time limits, and other procedural elements. The Order should be read and applied in light of the cited authorities and case law directing deference to reasonable agency conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, coordinated, and predictable environmental reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order enables DOT to conduct coordinated, consistent, predictable, and timely environmental reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should reduce unnecessary burdens and delays, expedite project delivery, and ensure reviews are completed in a timely manner across OAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote collaboration and efficiencies (early collaboration and dispute resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated Order promotes collaboration and efficiencies in the implementation of NEPA, encouraging early coordination, dispute resolution, and coordination techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should use early collaboration to streamline analyses and resolve issues before lengthy reviews; the Order expects adoption of such practices to reduce duplication and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase availability and use of Categorical Exclusions (CEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order increases the availability and use of CEs and provides processes that allow OAs to utilize each other's CEs and to adopt another agency's CEs in a streamlined manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although no OA CEs were modified in this Order, DOT plans to supplement and revise CEs in the near future; agencies should consider CEs where appropriate to avoid unnecessary EA/EIS preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on previously prepared EISs, EAs, and programmatic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order permits reliance on previously prepared EISs, EAs, and CEs and provides guidance for use of programmatic environmental review documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses from prior programmatic environmental review documents may be used in subsequent documents for a specified time period; agencies should follow the Order's direction when adopting or relying on prior analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for applicant-prepared environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order sets forth procedures for applicant-prepared environmental documents, including roles and responsibilities and the ability for a project sponsor to prepare an EA or EIS under agency supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prescribe procedures that govern applicant-prepared documents, define supervision and quality control, and clarify levels of NEPA review applicable to such documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and time limits for EAs and EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA 2023 established page and time limits for environmental assessments (EAs) and environmental impact statements (EISs); the Order implements these limits in its procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA documents prepared under DOT procedures must adhere to statutory page/time constraints; agencies should design reviews and scopes consistent with these limits to avoid unnecessary length and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited/streamlined analysis for multimodal and project delivery statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order reflects project delivery and streamlining provisions from SAFETEA-LU, MAP-21, the FAST Act, IIJA, and 23 U.S.C. 139, providing direction on analyzing multimodal projects in an expedited and streamlined manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAs should apply expedited processes and statutory authorities where applicable to accelerate decisionmaking for highway, transit, multimodal, and other delivery-focused projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated definitions: 'major Federal action' and related/connected actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order updates terminology, including the definition of 'major Federal action' and distinguishes between 'related actions' and 'connected actions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear definitions are provided to reduce ambiguity in scoping and applicability of NEPA review requirements across projects and OAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of OA as responsible entity for NEPA analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve readability and reduce ambiguity, the Order designates 'OA' as the entity responsible for conducting NEPA analyses and defines OA to include Secretarial Offices that carry out their own NEPA responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities, accountability, and who must act under the Order are tied to the OA designation; agencies must apply this structure when assigning tasks and decision roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and environmental review tracking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order incorporates environmental review tracking requirements and provides accountability mechanisms for agency compliance with NEPA as amended by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAs are expected to implement tracking and accountability systems to demonstrate timely progress and compliance; the Order's direction should be followed for departmental oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on significant issues; avoid generating paperwork
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order refocuses agency practice on fostering informed decisionmaking based on significant issues that require analysis, rather than generating paperwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA documents should concentrate analysis on genuinely significant environmental effects and avoid extensive treatment of trivial or attenuated issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded emergency environmental review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order expands DOT's emergency environmental review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for emergencies are clarified/expanded to allow appropriate expedited NEPA consideration when emergency circumstances arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retroactivity for sufficiently advanced ongoing NEPA reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised procedures will have no effect on sufficiently advanced ongoing NEPA reviews; DOT will continue to apply existing procedures to such reviews following CEQ guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects far along under prior procedures are 'grandfathered' and should not be forced to adopt the new Order's requirements mid-process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmentwide consistency with OA-specific flexibility (Subparts A-E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1-25 of the Order apply departmentwide, while Subparts A-E contain OA-specific procedures not covered by the departmentwide sections, allowing both consistency and OA-specific flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the departmentwide sections for general policy and consult OA subparts for OA-specific practices; many OA-level changes are non-substantive unless otherwise noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation and consolidation of prior DOT/OA NEPA orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order cancels DOT Order 5610.1C and cancels/incorporates multiple OA-specific NEPA implementing procedures into the new Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should treat the new Order as the interim authoritative procedure subject to future updates; references to canceled orders should be updated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of specific project types as major actions (MARAD example)
rubrics_metrics.description: MARAD-specific updates identify Deepwater Port license applications and large port infrastructure projects as major Federal actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAs may list particular project categories that require higher-level NEPA review; practitioners must consult OA-specific subparts for such identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for long-lead purchases and pre-NEPA field investigations for complex projects
rubrics_metrics.description: MARAD adds procedures specific to long-lead time purchases and pre-NEPA field investigations to clarify needs for complex projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where projects require procurement or investigations before NEPA completion, OAs should follow the specified procedures to manage risks while complying with NEPA timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on levels of NEPA review and their allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order clarifies levels of NEPA review (CE, EA, EIS), who determines the appropriate level, and how OA-specific CEs interact with departmentwide procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAs should apply the Order's criteria to determine the correct level of review and document rationale, including when using or adopting another OA's CE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of scope of EIS review and alternatives (FRA 2023 implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA 2023 limits the scope of 'major Federal action,' limits the scope of EIS review, and limits the alternatives that must be considered in an EIS; the Order implements those statutory limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA analyses should avoid expansive consideration of attenuated effects or excessively speculative alternatives inconsistent with statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission requirements and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted by the stated date (August 4, 2025); submissions must identify agency name, docket name, and docket number and be made via specified methods (regulations.gov, mail, hand delivery, fax); comments will be posted without change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should follow the instructions precisely (include docket number DOT-OST-2025-0171, use only one submission method, and note that personal information will be posted); late comments considered to the extent practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim effective date with opportunity for revision based on comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order is effective immediately upon publication as an interim order but may be updated based on comments received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Order is in effect immediately, agencies and stakeholders should recognize that changes may follow after public comment and further administrative action.
